summary: Independent initial audit of all 90 Chinese units, all 160 temporal or active-hint items, and all 41 extracted people. The review found recurrent ownership defects: dated appointments, posthumous honors, or ruler-era labels were copied to relatives and descriptive records without a personal dated event. It also found a point conversion that collapses the two named Tiancheng and Yingshun eras and a point death unsupported by 歲餘. The findings identify only affected temporal claims and hints; unrelated capture must remain intact.
